what: A background-color curtain covers the panel, with a noisy round hole (a droplet) cut in it so the scene below shows through. On load the hole opens from −.1 to .35 in 1s circ.out. Hovering the enter button swells it to .45 over .5s power2.out and it returns on release. Pressing opens it up to 1.5 over 5s expo.out and the curtain disappears. The hole’s edge ripples with simplex noise (size 15 · time ×.15) and (radius = progress² + noise × .1 × progress, in screen-width units), noise coordinates rotate by sin(progress)×2

options.open-dur: Opening length on entry (s), default 5 — shorten in the app
options.[data-fx-part=enter]: Button (child) that opens on press. If none, sends fx:open to the panel to open it

note: The curtain color is --kf-bg. The original multiplies a hole into the scene screen inside the scene post-processing, while the part cuts the same hole with an overlay curtain on top regardless of the scene. The shader was rewritten with the same formula by measuring the original (the original’s rotation constant could not be read from the bundle, so sin(progress)×2).

from.where: index.js irisMat (water-drop door: after loader −.1→.35 circ.out 1s · hover .45 · click 1.5 expo.out 5s)
